root_cause.text: The three new counter enumerations (BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR, BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR, BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS) were placed after BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR in the enum, which is used as the boundary marker for generic device stats allocation; this caused the generic stats array to be allocated with too few entries, leading to an out-of-bounds write in bnxt_re_copy_err_stats().
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message state: "BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR acts as a boundary marker for allocating hardware statistics with different num_counters values on chip_gen_p5_p7 devices. As a result, BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS are used when allocating hw_stats, which leads to an out-of-bounds write in bnxt_re_copy_err_stats()." The patch moves the three counters before BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR to include them in the generic counter set.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add new hardware error statistics counters for request and response CQE errors and remote access errors.
intent_record.what: Added three new enumerators to the bnxt_re_hw_stats enum: BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR, BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR, and BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS.
intent_record.how: Extends the hardware statistics enum to include additional error types, enabling the driver to track and report completion queue errors and remote access errors during RDMA operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove three invalid hardware statistics counters from bnxt_re driver enumeration.
intent_record.what: Removed three enum members (BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR, BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR, BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS) from the bnxt_re_hw_stats enumeration.
intent_record.how: The removal reduces the value of BNXT_RE_NUM_EXT_COUNTERS by 3, causing any code that iterates over extended counters or allocates arrays based on that value to skip these three indices. The driver will no longer attempt to report or handle these specific statistics.

candidates.rationale: This new enumeration was placed after BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR, which is used as the boundary for generic stats allocation; the array size does not include this index, causing out-of-bounds write.

vuln_statements.explanation: This enumeration constant was placed after BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR in the enum, which serves as the boundary marker for generic device statistics allocation. As a result, the generic stats array is allocated with fewer entries than needed, causing an out-of-bounds write when bnxt_re_copy_err_stats() accesses this index.

This enumeration constant was placed after BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR, causing the generic stats array allocation to be too small. Accessing this index in bnxt_re_copy_err_stats() results in an out-of-bounds write.
